chadi-init.description: Initialize or refresh the current repo with agent-chadi workflow files.
chadi-init.template: Use agent-chadi. Initialize this project if missing, otherwise refresh only missing .opencode/chadi workflow files. Use AGENTS.md and .opencode only. Do not create CLAUDE.md or .claude.

chadi-fast.description: DEFAULT mode. Main-agent-first workflow. Standard work auto-proceeds; Heavy work waits for approval unless pre-approved.
chadi-fast.template: Use agent-chadi. chadi-fast mode — classify the lane first, then dispatch the matching squad as parallel task calls in ONE tool-call block. Trivial stays inline. Main agent still owns tests, security checklist, diff review, and the final verified report. Standard work auto-proceeds; Heavy work waits for approval unless user already pre-approved.

chadi-review.description: Run final testing, security review, and code review.
chadi-review.template: Use agent-chadi. Run testing review, security review, and final code review. Update .opencode/chadi logs.

chadi-plan.description: Create an industry-style plan with risk classification and parallel execution plan.
chadi-plan.template: Use agent-chadi. Do intake, acceptance criteria, discovery, architecture map, risk classification, and PARALLEL_PLAN.md. Use matching skills and available codegraph/context7 tools when relevant. Do not implement yet unless the user already asked to proceed.

chadi-waves.description: Plan a multi-layer feature as parallel waves (contract -> builders -> integration -> verify -> deploy) and dispatch wave 0.
chadi-waves.template: Use agent-chadi. Call graphyloop_plan_feature with the user's request as the goal. Report the wave table (which lanes run in parallel, what each owns, what gates the deploy), then pass plan.tasks to graphyloop_distribute and dispatch ONLY the tasks it returns in dispatchNow — wave 0 freezes the contract alone. After each result, graphyloop_record it and dispatch whatever that unblocked, all tasks of a wave in ONE tool-call block. Do not let a builder start before the contract file exists.

chadi-db.description: Set up or migrate the database (Supabase-first): check credentials, plan migrations, dry-run before apply.
chadi-db.template: Use agent-chadi. Database setup lane. 1) graphyloop_secrets_status to see which Supabase keys exist — never ask the user to paste a key into the chat; if one is missing, tell them the exact key name and where to get it, then store it with graphyloop_secrets_set. 2) graphyloop_env_sync so the app reads real credentials from its own env file. 3) graphyloop_preflight target=db and clear every blocker. 4) Write schema changes as migration files (never dashboard-only edits), with RLS policies and indexes. 5) Run the dry-run step and show its SQL BEFORE any apply; the apply step needs explicit user approval and a rollback note. Never print a credential value.

chadi-deploy.description: Ship to Vercel safely: preflight, mirror env keys, preview deploy, then gated production.
chadi-deploy.template: Use agent-chadi. Deploy lane. 1) graphyloop_preflight target=deploy — every blocker must be cleared first (missing VERCEL_TOKEN, no build script, env file not git-ignored). 2) Mirror every runtime env key in the Vercel project; a local .env.local is not deployed. 3) Apply pending database migrations before the app deploy, dry-run first, with a rollback note. 4) Run the local build, then a PREVIEW deployment and verify the real URL. 5) Production deploy only after explicit user approval, and record the rollback command in the report. Never print a credential value.

chadi-audit.description: Run testing, security, performance, and final code review without broad implementation.
chadi-audit.template: Use agent-chadi. Audit the project or current changes. Run testing review, security review, performance/reliability review when relevant, and final code review. Update .opencode/chadi logs.

chadi-release.description: Prepare release notes, rollback plan, and final verification summary.
chadi-release.template: Use agent-chadi. Prepare release notes, rollback plan, risk register update, verification summary, and final checks for the current work.

chadi-skills.description: Scan installed original OpenCode skills and update agent-chadi skill source map.
chadi-skills.template: Use agent-chadi. Inspect installed original skills from .opencode/skills, ~/.config/opencode/skills, ~/.opencode/skills, and project-local .opencode/skills. Update CHADI_SKILL_SOURCES.md. Do not fake missing ECC or Superpowers skills. Do not create Claude files.

chadi-research.description: Use last30days for fresh public internet/community research before answering.
chadi-research.template: Use agent-chadi. Use the installed last30days skill as source-of-truth for fresh public internet research. Research the user's topic from the last 30 days, then answer with grounded summary and cite/summarize the evidence. If last30days is missing or fails, report that and use the closest available fallback.

chadi-confusing.description: For confusing/current questions, research first using last30days, then answer.
chadi-confusing.template: Use agent-chadi. The user is asking something confusing or likely recent. Before answering, check whether last30days is installed. If available, use it to research current public context. If not available, say what fallback you used. Then answer clearly.

chadi-discuss.description: Discuss-first mode: parallel discovery then present plan, wait for approval before implementing.
chadi-discuss.template: Use agent-chadi in DISCUSS-FIRST mode. Inspect only needed files with batched tools. Present a concise plan: lane chosen, what I'll do, files touched, approach, risks, optional parallel work if warranted, and verification plan. WAIT for user approval before implementing. Do NOT implement until the user says go/proceed/approved.

chadi-go.description: Skip discuss gate, straight to main-agent implementation.
chadi-go.template: Use agent-chadi. User pre-approved — skip DISCUSS-FIRST GATE. Classify the lane, dispatch the matching squad as parallel task calls in ONE tool-call block, then run tests, security checklist, and final diff review in the main loop. Update logs when relevant and report verified results.

chadi-recall.description: PMB memory recall — search facts, lessons, decisions, goals, past activity.
chadi-recall.template: Use agent-chadi. Query PMB for the user's topic: (1) pmb_recall(query) for structured facts/rules/lessons/decisions/goals; (2) pmb_project_overview if a known project. Synthesize results. If the pmb_* tools are not loaded (the pmb MCP is currently disabled in opencode.json), fall back to graphyloop_memory_search and state which backend answered. PMB is the preferred memory system — no agentmemory. If PMB returns nothing, say so, don't fabricate.
